messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/generate (hosted). p99 preproc latency > 2.2s for the last 5m, p95 ~420ms. Paging @oncall group. Possible streaming stalls reported by downstream clients.

jordan-oncall: taking pager. pinging riley + sam to triage. any recent deploys to preproc or prompt pipeline?

riley-sre: saw a deploy to preproc-worker pool ~10m ago from ci (sha: d1f4b7). Noted an A/B for new prompt-template caching.

sam-ml: also seeing increased CPU in tokenizer process on several hosts. JSON-mode requests have higher tail.

jordan-oncall: ok stack: preproc -> tokenizer -> template-expander -> streaming-router. Symptoms: streaming tail stalls + p99 preproc spike. Customer visible errors: increased streaming timeouts and partial responses.

leo-support: multiple customers reported streaming disconnects around 12:01 UTC, severity high for two enterprise tenants.

riley-sre: metrics snapshot (last 10m): p95=420ms, p99=2.4s, error rate streaming=1.5% -> baseline 0.3%. KB: streaming tail latency at +1.6s on affected requests.

sam-ml: correlating traces: longest traces hit prompt-template parsing with tool schema expansion + JSON-mode parsing path. High variability when templates include nested tool schemas and large example blocks.

jordan-oncall: can you paste a representative trace/log?

sam-ml: here’s a truncated log from a slow request:
```
[12:02:10.123] preproc: start request id=req_9a7c
[12:02:10.124] tokenizer: tokenizing input size=18k chars, mode=json
[12:02:10.890] template-expander: expanding tool schemas (n=6), resolving defaults
[12:02:12.560] preproc: streaming handoff delayed, kv-cache warmup blocked
[12:02:12.600] preproc: finish request id=req_9a7c duration=2.477s
```

jordan-oncall: tokenizer duration ~760ms, template expansion ~1.67s — that's the tail. Any recent changes to JSON-mode parsing or schema validation libs?

riley-sre: yes, we bumped a dependency (json-schema-validator v4.1.0) in the template path last week for stricter validation. Could be slower on deeply nested schemas.

anya-pm: affected customers use our JSON-mode for tool-calling heavy flows. They rely on streaming for responsiveness. Need quick mitigation to restore SLOs.

jordan-oncall: mitigation options: 1) rollback the template caching deploy, 2) disable JSON-mode path for hosted (quick config flip), 3) route traffic to fallback model variant with simpler prompt path, 4) soft-rate-limit large template requests. Which is fastest?

riley-sre: fastest is config flip to disable JSON-mode parsing for hosted (no restart). We can also enable fallback routing for customers with >10s tails.

sam-ml: disabling JSON-mode will avoid heavy schema validation/expansion, but some clients expect structured outputs — warn support.

jordan-oncall: do it. riley, flip JSON-mode to off for hosted region us-east-1. sam, prepare rollback of json-schema bump if needed. leo, craft customer-facing note.

riley-sre: making the change now: `kubectl set env deployment/preproc-frontend JSON_MODE=false --namespace=prod-us-east-1`

deploy-bot: Deployment event: set env JSON_MODE=false on preproc-frontend (prod-us-east-1) by riley-sre at 12:10:23 UTC. No pod restarts required.

jordan-oncall: monitoring...

riley-sre: immediate numbers post-flip (2m window): p95=380ms, p99=560ms, streaming error rate down to 0.45%. p99 improved a lot.

sam-ml: traces show template-expander time dropped to ~120ms when JSON-mode short-circuited. Tokenizer CPU still a bit high on big payloads, but well under SLO.

leo-support: drafted message for affected tenants: "We detected elevated streaming latency due to a pre-processing path for JSON-mode templates. We've temporarily disabled JSON-mode for hosted traffic in your region to restore responsiveness. We're investigating a permanent fix." Want approval before sending.

anya-pm: send now, mark as incident in status page and include ETA for next update in 1h.

jordan-oncall: ok incident severity lowered; but root cause unknown: dependency perf + increased usage of nested tool-schemas + a recent deploy. Action items assigned: riley -> revert dependency bump and run perf tests in staging; sam -> optimize template-expander caching and lazy-schema-resolve; infra -> add fallback routing policy for heavy-template requests; support -> customer comms; oncall -> follow for 1h then handoff.

jordan-oncall: preparing handoff to next oncall @riley-sre at 13:00 UTC. Summary for handoff:
- issue: preproc p99 spike caused by JSON-mode template expansion + json-schema validator bump
- impact: streaming stalls, partial responses, 1.5% streaming error rate at peak, 2 enterprise customers affected
- mitigation applied: JSON_MODE=false flip (prod-us-east-1) at 12:10:23 UTC, p99 reduced to ~560ms
- next steps: revert lib bump in staging, run perf matrix for nested schemas, implement request-size rate limits for template-expansion path, follow-up postmortem ticket.

riley-sre: taking handoff. I'll continue with revert + perf tests. Leaving notes and links to traces in the incident ticket.

incidents-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-4387. Severity: Sev2 -> downgraded to Sev3 after mitigation. Assigned: riley-sre, sam-ml, leo-support. Next update due in 60 minutes.

jordan-oncall: thanks team. handing off now. I'll be available if escalation needed.

riley-sre: ack. I'll follow up with timeline and root-cause analysis.

leo-support: sent customer notifications at 12:18 UTC, included workarounds and support contact.

sam-ml: quick note — adding a cheap circuit-breaker to skip deep schema validation for requests with >5 nested schemas could prevent recurrence. I'll propose PR.

jordan-oncall: ended handoff.

incidents-bot: Handoff recorded: from=jordan-oncall to=riley-sre at 13:00:00 UTC.

riley-sre: last message before next update: perf test plan scheduled, will validate rollback path and can re-enable JSON_MODE in a controlled canary once fixed.

incidents-bot: Thread closed for active paging. All follow-ups moved to INC-2026-4387 and postmortem board.
